title: How to Get an Okta API Token and Handle Rate Limits
summary: The Okta API included with your org has no per-call charge, so you can build requests to the Users endpoint and handle rate limits without extra fees.
body_markdown:
## Okta API rate limits by plan and endpoint


Okta sets rate limits per endpoint group rather than as one number for the whole API. The remaining count you watch while paging through users is a different budget from the one your token requests draw on.


### Limits per endpoint and plan tier


Three of the four endpoints sit at **600 requests per minute** per org, and only the OAuth token endpoint is higher, so the lower three define your effective rate-limit floor.


According to[APIs.io](https://apis.io/rate-limits/okta/okta-rate-limits/) ,` /api/v1/users` and` /api/v1/apps` each allow 600 requests per minute, which means exceeding this limit results in throttling. A full user sync and an app inventory job therefore draw from separate buckets and won't starve each other.


At 1000 requests per minute, the` /oauth2/v1/token` endpoint is unlikely to be your bottleneck unless you request a fresh token per call instead of caching it.


The logs endpoint is the tightest at **120 requests per minute** , so a log poller needs a longer interval and larger page sizes than a user sync would.


Those figures are per org, not per API token. Every integration sharing an org shares the same budget, and a nightly job can eat into what an interactive tool needs.


Limits also vary by plan tier, so confirm your own numbers in the Admin Console rather than assuming these apply unchanged.


### Reading the rate limit headers


Every response carries three headers:` x-rate-limit-limit` (the ceiling for that bucket),` x-rate-limit-remaining` (calls left in the current window) and` x-rate-limit-reset` (when the window resets, as epoch seconds).


Read them on every response, not only on failures. Once remaining drops below a threshold you choose, sleep until the reset time instead of firing the next call and collecting a 429.


When a 429 does arrive, the same reset header tells you how long to wait. Retrying immediately just spends budget on calls that will fail again. Because each endpoint group has its own bucket, track these values per endpoint, not as one global counter.


### The org-wide limit and concurrency limits


Beyond the per-endpoint buckets, Okta applies an org-wide limit across all API traffic and a separate concurrency limit on simultaneous in-flight requests.


A burst of parallel workers can trip the concurrency limit even when your per-minute counts look healthy, so cap your worker pool instead of relying on the per-minute headers alone.


The Admin Console rate limit dashboard shows which buckets are being hit and when. When a 429 appears that your headers can't explain, check the dashboard first, since another integration in the same org is the usual cause.
